Reduced prime-boost antibody kinetics

Source: R/model_andraud.R
andraud_trajectory.Rd

A reduced form of the plasma-cell and antibody model of Andraud et al. (2012), in which antibody is produced by a short-lived and a long-lived source and cleared at rate \(m_A\): $$\dot S = -m_s S, \qquad \dot A = W_l + S - m_A A,$$ with \(S(0) = W_s\) and \(A(0) = A_0\). Solving gives a sum of three exponentials, and at the boost the two fluxes receive increments, so the trajectory is continuous there by construction.

Usage

andraud_trajectory(
  t,
  A0,
  C1,
  C2,
  D1,
  D2,
  ms,
  mA = log(2)/(26/30),
  t_boost = 84/30,
  floor_at = 0.01
)

Arguments

t

Times in months since the prime.

A0, C1, C2, D1, D2

Levels on the titre scale: baseline, prime-only plateau and its short-lived amplitude, post-boost plateau and its short-lived amplitude.

ms

Decay rate of the short-lived source, per month.

mA

Antibody clearance rate, per month. The default corresponds to an IgG half-life of about 26 days.

t_boost

Time of the boost, months since the prime.

floor_at

Value at which non-positive predictions are floored. A sum of exponentials with mixed signs is not constrained positive; pass -Inf to inspect the raw solution, which is what a positivity screen needs.

Value

A numeric vector of antibody concentration at t.

Details

The three levels the classes are built on are read straight off the model. \(A_0\) is the initial condition; setting \(\dot A = 0\) once the short-lived source is spent gives the prime-only plateau \(C_1 = W_l / m_A\); the same argument after the boost gives \(D_1 = (W_l + \Delta W_l)/m_A\). The transient peak four weeks after the boost reflects \(\Delta W_s\) and decays, so it is not the durable level.

Holding \(W_l\) constant is what makes the plateaus well defined. It is reasonable over a study of this length: antibody clearance is fast, yet antibody to vaccine antigens persists for decades, which given that clearance rate requires continuing production.

References

Andraud M et al. (2012) Living on three time scales: the dynamics of plasma cell and antibody populations. PLoS Comput Biol 8, e1002418.

See also

amp_to_flux(), andraud_levels()

Examples

round(andraud_trajectory(c(0, 1, 2.8, 3.7, 14), A0 = 400, C1 = 1200,
                         C2 = 0, D1 = 3000, D2 = 2500, ms = 0.3))
#> [1]  400  840 1115 2774 3086
